column1: Mimicking

The next priority of my budget is to do everything possible to protect our citizens and strengthen our nation against the ongoing threat of another attack. We face a new kind of enemy, one that hates freedom and despises America. This enemy has attacked our nation and our way of life, and we will respond. We will meet this threat and defend our country. We will not yield. We will not be intimidated. America will never be intimidated by terrorists.

In addition to these important -- to these management changes, we should move forward with other reforms to make the IMF and World Bank more transparent, accountable, and effective. These institutions must be held to high standards, and their resources must be used wisely. We must ensure that the aid that is provided reaches the people it is intended to help – and there are some specific steps we can take to achieve these goals.

Yet we are a different nation today -- sadder and stronger, less innocent and more courageous, more appreciative of life, and for many who serve our country, more willing to risk life in a great cause. We will not forget the events of that day -- September 11, 2001. The memory of those who were lost, and the resolve of those who survived, serves as a constant reminder to the country: We must confront the evil. May God bless the United States of America.

We are engaged in the defining ideological struggle of the 21st century. The terrorists oppose every principle of humanity and decency that we hold dear. They seek to deny freedom to others, while they themselves are slaves to ideology. But the American people are not slaves; we are free. We answer to our own conscience, and we answer to a higher power as well.

What I am proposing tonight is the most extensive reorganization of the federal government since the 1940s. To win the Cold War, President Truman united military forces under a single Department of Defense. That action helped the United States to achieve victory over its adversaries, and today we face a different kind of war. This new war requires new structures and new strategies, and that is why I am proposing the creation of a new Department of Homeland Security.

Fourth, the new law will help all Americans pay for out-of-pocket health costs. This legislation also helps secure the economic future of the middle class by offering tax credits for health insurance, and by expanding access to health savings accounts. We will strengthen Medicare, and we will work to improve our nation's health-care system. This plan is comprehensive and will benefit every single American.

The gravest danger to freedom lies at the perilous crossroads of radicalism and technology. When dictators gain weapons of mass destruction, they will be able to blackmail the free world. Therefore, we will continue to confront dangers before they fully materialize. We will encourage a world in which the oppressed can choose their own destiny, and we'll work to defeat those who terrorize others. The nation must stand firm, because our security depends upon the success of liberty in all nations.

It costs a lot to fight this war. We have spent more than $1 billion a week to defend our country. We are fighting this war because we must. But we can not achieve victory unless we also promote economic growth here at home. Our economy is strong, but it could be stronger. And we must make it stronger.

Reaching this moment has not been easy, as you could tell from Chairman Boehner's discussion. We've overcome a lot. We face continuing challenges. Our nation is at war. I know the cost of war; I see it in the faces of the wounded, and I feel it in the grief of the families who’ve lost loved ones. But as our nation confronts these and other challenges, we must remain confident in our vision.

Competition between great nations is inevitable, but armed conflict in our world is not. More More and more, the civilized world is choosing peace over war. And together, we are building a more peaceful world. The values of liberty are universal. The desire to be free is present in every human heart. And eventually, the voices of freedom will be heard.

It has been the privilege of a lifetime to serve as your President. There have been moments of joy and moments of sorrow. Through it all, I have tried my best to lead our country with conviction and compassion. Today, the American people can be proud of the progress we have made together. We have confronted adversity, we have shown resilience, and we have kept the faith. America is stronger and more confident because of it.

Historians in the future will reflect on an extraordinary, undeniable fact: Over time, free nations are more likely to be stable and peaceful nations. They are less likely to be the sources of conflict, and more likely to be partners in solving the problems of the world. The advance of freedom is the surest strategy to protect our nation and our friends from the threats of terror. We’ve got a lot of work to do, and we will not rest until the job is done.

The third element of a comprehensive reform is to hold employers accountable for the workers they hire, and to make sure that the documents they provide are real. We will not allow employers to be indifferent to the law. This is a fundamental step to secure our borders. America will be stronger as a result of these reforms.

It's also essential for the many organizations of our country to reach out to your communities with compassion and understanding. We've learned from this tragedy and are now able to act from the knowledge gained. It is America’s duty to provide aid to those who are hurting and to work toward a peaceful world. America has a responsibility to lead, and, thankfully, we have allies.

And, finally, the civilized world faces a grave threat from weapons of mass destruction. A As we meet tonight, the proliferation of these weapons -- and the means to deliver them -- is of growing concern. The attacks of September 11 showed what terrorists can do with the weapons they have. We cannot allow terrorists and terrorist states to threaten America with weapons of mass destruction. We must act now.

Every time I'm invited to this rostrum, I'm humbled by the privilege and mindful of the responsibilities of this office. The American people have entrusted me with a great task, and it is my duty to report on the state of our Union. We face challenges, great and serious challenges. However, we are also a nation of resolute purpose and enormous capacity for progress.

I propose a new temporary worker program that will match willing foreign workers with willing employers for jobs Americans are not doing. I call on Congress to create this program. Also, I want to increase border security. We must know who comes in, who goes out, and why. We must also hold employers to account.

A simple chemical reaction between hydrogen and oxygen generates energy, which can be used to power our homes, businesses, and cars. Imagine a world less dependent on foreign sources of energy, a world where we can power our economy with clean, renewable sources. This vision is within our reach, and we must strive to achieve it. It begins by focusing on innovation, research, and development. By doing so, we'll create new jobs and invigorate our economy.

In all these areas--from the disruption of terror networks, to victory in Iraq, to the --to an economy that is growing and providing jobs, we see the progress, and we will build on it. We will build on that progress to achieve a safer America.

Historians will note that in many nations, the advance of markets and free enterprise helped to create conditions for greater freedom. A clear path to opportunity opened to millions. In the 21st century, it is essential that we seize the opportunities before us. We must advance liberty and prosperity in every corner of the world. And by doing so, we will make America safer and more secure.

America's immigration system is also outdated--unsuited to the needs of our economy and to the values of our country. We need an immigration policy that reflects the character of America: a nation that welcomes talented, hard-working people, and a nation that stands for fairness. To fix our broken immigration system, we must have a comprehensive approach. It should include: border security, a temporary worker program, and a way for those who are here legally to earn citizenship.

My administration understood that America could not retreat in the face of terror. And we understood that our best weapon against terror is a strategy of robust action. We pursued a comprehensive strategy to protect America, to prevent attacks before they happen, and to deny terrorists the space, the resources, and the support they need to operate. We sought to change the conditions that give rise to terror by promoting freedom and hope in the world.

The story of children being just shuffled through the system is one of the saddest stories I know. We have to change this. We need to encourage them to pursue their dreams and provide them with the skills they need to succeed. We must ensure that every child has access to a quality education, and that no child is left behind. This is a moral imperative, and it is crucial to our future.

Our national courage has been clear in times of depression and war, when defending common ideals has required great sacrifice. The same spirit of sacrifice is now required to confront the threat of terrorism. We will not waver. We will not tire. We will not allow terrorists to change our way of life. We are a nation determined to fight this evil, and we will prevail. We are building a world that is more secure, and more free.

Our first goal is clear: We must have an economy that grows fast enough to create good jobs for every American who wants one. And to achieve this goal, we must pursue policies that encourage economic growth. We must do more to expand trade, to cut taxes and regulations, and to promote economic opportunity. We must continue to improve our education system so that every child can learn to read and write and add and subtract.

Good morning. For years, America's automakers have faced serious challenges -- burdensome costs, a shrinking market share, growing foreign competition. The financial crisis has only made things worse. The situation is urgent. And the stakes are enormous. The auto industry is central to the economic well-being of this country. So we must act.

I have confidence in the promise of America because I know the character of our country. We are a nation that values faith, family, and freedom. We are a nation of compassion that faces adversity with courage and resolve. We are a nation of optimism, and we believe in the power of the human spirit. In about two years, full prescription coverage under Medicare will begin. In return for a modest monthly premium, seniors will get the peace of mind of knowing their medicine costs will be covered. This is one of the most important benefits in the history of Medicare. And as the first step toward this goal, we’re working to fully fund the budget for the National Institutes of Health. The NIH is the leading medical research institution in the world, and America should lead the way in discovering cutting-edge cures for diseases.

America rejects the false comfort of isolationism. We are the nation that saved liberty in Europe. We are the nation that helped lift the iron curtain. We are the nation that welcomes immigrants, respects the rights of all, and upholds the rule of law. We fight for the ideals of free people because we know that in the long run, those ideals are the world's only sure defense. America will continue to lead, and we will prevail.

We've worked with our nation's governors to deploy 6,000 National Guard members to provide the support at airports and our borders. We have invested billions of dollars to protect ports and critical infrastructure. We're working to improve preparedness at the local level. And we're working closely with our allies to disrupt terrorist financing and to share intelligence and to bring the terrorists to justice. We must be relentless.

America is a nation with a mission, and that mission comes from our most basic commitments. We believe every person is created equal, and worthy of human dignity. We believe every life is precious, and every life has potential. This belief is at the heart of American ideals and the spirit of the American people. We believe everyone deserves liberty, opportunity, and justice.

Once we have funded our national security and our homeland security, the final great priority of the budget is meeting our obligations to the American people. We will continue to support our commitment to education, and continue to reform it. I support reforms that empower parents, high standards, and local control. We will meet our commitment to our seniors. We will keep the promises of Medicare. We will continue to make sure our military men and women have the resources they need.

The world has waited 12 years for Iraq to disarm. America will not accept a threat to our security, and we will not stand by as Saddam Hussein violates his obligations, and abandons the pursuit of peace. The United Nations Security Council has given Iraq a final chance to disarm. The United States hopes Iraq will meet its obligations. Should Iraq fail to disarm, the United States, with the United Nations, will disarm Iraq.

In the rebuilding process, there will be many important decisions and many details to resolve, but as we work to rebuild our nation, the ultimate goal for all of us must be to build a better America. An America dedicated to the values of human dignity, personal responsibility, and individual liberty -- and a nation that is committed to building a culture of service and compassion. It is a task worthy of our great nation.

With us today are 15 of the many families I met as I toured our nation after September the 11th, 2001. These families showed the world the true character of America: resilient, compassionate, and strong. They had suffered an unspeakable loss, yet they found the strength to go on -- to comfort others, and to serve something greater than themselves. And in their example, we find the courage to confront the enemy. And in their courage, we find the determination to win the war on terror.

To overcome dangers in our world, we must also take the offensive by encouraging economic growth and development. By opening markets and expanding trade, we will advance our strategic interests. Trade creates new opportunities for American businesses and workers, and it lifts lives in the developing world. Economic freedom is essential to human progress. And when nations open their economies, they also open their societies to the forces of reform and the hope of democracy. We must continue to work with our friends and allies to advance this vision.

Defeatism may have its partisan uses, but it is not justified by the facts. For For America and for the world, the central challenge of our time is to fight and win the war on terror. We must pursue the terrorists wherever they hide, and we must deny them the sanctuary and support they rely on. We must also confront the ideologies of hatred that incite terrorism. We will not yield, and we will not be intimidated.

A hopeful society gives special attention to children who lack direction and love. Through the work of faith-based and community programs, we must help troubled children. We must show these children that America cares. We will help them by providing mentors to guide and support them. Mentors who know that the heart of America, the soul of America, is good. We must also support parents and help them create an ideal environment for their kids.

Inside the United States, where the war began, we must continue to give our homeland security professionals the tools they need to defend our country. We must pursue every lead, and disrupt every plot, and bring every terrorist to justice. My administration is committed to do that. We must continue to make sure our system of justice serves the needs of our nation.

Tonight, I propose a permanent Cabinet-level Department of Homeland Security to unite essential agencies that Now, I believe, must work together to protect America. This new department will have a clear mission: to protect the American homeland. It will coordinate the efforts of 22 agencies and 170,000 employees. These agencies include those responsible for border security, disaster relief, chemical and biological threats, and the Coast Guard, among others. We have an obligation to make sure that our homeland is secure.

We're working with Yemen's government to prevent terrorists from reassembling there. We sent troops to the Philippines to help them fight terror. We're working with Indonesia to help them fight terror. We're helping the Afghan people build a free society. The United States of America will not sit idly by as threats gather. We will confront them. And we will defeat them. And we will stand strong for freedom.

In the aftermath, we have seen fellow citizens left stunned and uprooted, searching for loved ones. We have seen the rescuers -- brave men and women -- facing unimaginable risks. We've seen America rise to its feet.

And now, we are challenged to defend our country in a new and different way. Because with every passing day, the memory of September 11th fades for some. But the resolve of our nation must not. We will never forget the lessons of that day, nor will we falter in our duty to protect the American people.
